additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia Nervosa is characterized by recurrent episodes of eating unusually large amounts of food with a sense of loss of control, followed by compensatory behaviors such as self-induced purging, with self-evaluation strongly tied to weight or shape. It often develops over months to years, may be hidden because weight can remain in a socially expected range, and is distinguished from anorexia nervosa by the absence of persistently significantly low body weight as the defining feature.

patient.stressor_event: Spouse beginning or ceasing work outside the home
patient.stressor: When Jennifer’s husband stopped working outside the home and was suddenly around the house most days, her long-standing routines around baking, walking club, and carefully planned meals became less private and more emotionally charged. Over the next 7 months, she became increasingly preoccupied with how her weight and shape reflected on her at church events, bridge league, and the retail store, while episodes of eating far more than intended began occurring after potlucks or late shifts. She then developed a repeated pattern of purging afterward to avoid weight gain, keeping it hidden behind her sociable, capable image. She came to psychiatric care after a primary care visit for general health monitoring led to a more direct discussion about eating patterns, and she accepted a referral when she realized the behavior had become established rather than occasional.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.
S048.manifestation: What finally scared me into coming in is that after I eat too much, I’ve been making myself throw up in the bathroom so I won’t gain weight, and it’s gotten to where it isn’t just a one-time mistake anymore.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: If my skirt feels tight before church or I catch my side view in the store mirror, it can ruin my whole day because I feel like everyone can tell I’ve let myself go.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: After a bridge night or a late shift, I might come home and eat leftover casserole, cookies I baked, crackers, and ice cream all in one sitting, much more than I’d ever put on a plate in front of anyone.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start during those times, it feels like I’m on automatic, thinking I should stop before my husband notices but still reaching for one more thing.

add_requirements.The binge eating and inappropriate compe: For at least the past several months, it’s been happening most weeks that I have one of those secret eating spells and then go make myself sick afterward. I can’t honestly call it occasional anymore.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’m still showing up for work, church, and bridge, but I’ve started planning my day around avoiding certain foods or getting home alone afterward. It makes social things feel tense instead of enjoyable.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about seven months, since my husband stopped working outside the home and my routines stopped feeling private.
